comparison: Perfect agreement on Tus-TerB binding claims (C2-C6, C32). Both evaluations find the evidence from ChIP-qPCR, PLA, and sequencing convincing and sufficient to demonstrate specific binding in human cells.
Perfect agreement on background claims (C1, C7, C51, C74, C75) about the Tus-TerB system from prior work. Both acknowledge these as established context supported by appropriate citations.

Strong agreement on background/established knowledge claims (C16, C23, C30-C31, C46, C64-C73). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited prior work providing necessary context. OpenEval includes C79 which peer review addresses separately.

Strong agreement on fork stalling evidence (C8-C12, C33, C78) from SMARD data. Both find the evidence compelling for site-specific replication block. OpenEval also includes MCM3/FANCM ChIP data (C13-C15) which peer review evaluates separately in R3.

Overlap on MCM3 and FANCM ChIP data (C13-C15, C57). Both evaluations support these as orthogonal evidence for fork stalling. Peer review groups these separately from SMARD data, while OpenEval combines them.

Strong agreement on localized γH2AX accumulation (C17-C19, C35-C36). Both evaluations find the ChIP-qPCR and PLA data convincing for demonstrating localized response at the RFB site. OpenEval also includes comparison to Cas9 (C20-C22) which peer review evaluates separately.
Partial overlap on C20 (Cas9 comparison). OpenEval includes this with localized γH2AX data, while peer review emphasizes it as a key distinction between DSB and fork stalling responses.

Agreement on the distinction between localized and spreading γH2AX responses (C42-C43). Both evaluations support the contrast between Tus-TerB (localized, ATR-dependent) and Cas9-induced DSB (spreading). OpenEval provides more mechanistic detail about ATM vs ATR.

Strong agreement on lack of global checkpoint activation (C24-C25, C38-C39). Both evaluations confirm the absence of ATR-T1989, CHK1-S345, and RPA2-S33 phosphorylation, contrasting with HU treatment. OpenEval also includes ATRi experiments (C26-C28, C40) which peer review evaluates separately.

Agreement on ATR-dependence of localized γH2AX response (C27-C28, C40). Both evaluations confirm ATRi experiments demonstrate ATR-dependence. Peer review emphasizes this as key evidence, while OpenEval groups it with broader checkpoint activation data.
Partial overlap on C21 (lack of global γH2AX signal). OpenEval includes this with localized response data, while peer review uses it to contrast with HU-induced global response.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C34, C61, C63, C76-C77) about localized ATR-dependent checkpoint response distinct from global responses. Both evaluations find the overall model well-supported by the collective data. Peer review also includes C43 which OpenEval evaluates in R8.

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic claims (C29, C49-C50, C62). Both evaluations recognize these as speculative about downstream consequences and future directions rather than directly demonstrated findings. Peer review also includes C45, C58-C60 as speculative.

Agreement on uncertainty of ATR activation mechanism (C44-C45, C79). Both evaluations recognize this as a hypothesis requiring future investigation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct evidence; peer review does not explicitly evaluate but notes mechanistic details remain to be determined.

Partial agreement on RFB resolution mechanisms (C52-C55). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to reliance on yeast data and lack of direct demonstration in human cells. Peer review groups these with other discussion points and affirms the overall system's utility without specifically challenging the resolution mechanism claims.

Agreement on FANCM enrichment (C57). OpenEval rates the enrichment as supported but notes uncertainty about mechanistic details (C58-C59). Peer review explicitly confirms FANCM ChIP data as valid evidence for fork stalling.

Agreement on uncertainty about temporal relationships and mechanistic details (C58-C59). Both evaluations recognize these as areas requiring further investigation. OpenEval explicitly rates as UNCERTAIN; peer review notes 'it is unclear for how long forks remain stalled.'

Agreement on C41 citing prior yeast work. Both evaluations accept this as appropriate comparative context. OpenEval evaluates separately as SUPPORTED background; peer review includes with discussion claims.
Agreement on C60 as future direction. OpenEval explicitly identifies this as appropriately framed future work. Peer review groups with other speculative claims without specific challenge.

OpenEval rates C37 (torsional stress mechanism for localized γH2AX) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this mechanistic claim.
